b801afa2-2f44-487f-a0d1-c2b0af334df6.description: Recover the policy program embedded in the retained rules compiler and identify the input it actually evaluates.

hints.text: Read work/build-operations/policy-compiler-handoff.md on the developer workstation. It directs you to the fieldkest/policy-compiler repository in Gitea (source.keplerops.test). Clone it; the repository website field points to the client reference on source-tools.keplerops.test:8443 where the evaluation route is listed.

The retained binary is an unstripped ELF; binary analysis with nm reveals the eight fieldkest_opcode_XX_NAME symbols. Search the binary for the FKPC magic bytes (the embedded 68-byte program table, 14 four-byte instructions). Trace the PUSH_FIELD opcodes by index to identify the four evaluated fields — tenant_state (0), connector_api (1), signer_lineage (2), compatibility_exception (3).

Build a fieldkest.policy-program-model/v1 with the 68-byte program base64-encoded and its sha256. Submit it to the policy-compiler evaluation route on source-tools.keplerops.test with operation=corpus-check and the corpus_id from the README. The service returns a PCMIG receipt with program_sha256 and condition_set_sha256.

643dfe55-613f-4ec6-8b36-3350d0061946.name: K11.2: Learn its instructions
643dfe55-613f-4ec6-8b36-3350d0061946.description: Reconstruct enough of the compiler's internal instruction behavior to reproduce the supplied policy fragments.

hints.text: The fieldkest/policy-compiler repository README describes each fragment's policy intent in the Fragments section. No .fkpc bytecode is provided — the participant must assemble each fragment. Use the FKPC encoding from K11.1 (magic plus header plus 4-byte instructions). PUSH_FIELD operand is field index 0-3; PUSH_CONST is constant index; IN_SET is set index; each set and constant value is in the README.

hints.text: Navigate to FUXA (hmi.arwc.test) and open the Cairn Reach overview. The view shows live level, usable volume, two outlet positions (%), two outlet flows (m3/s), total flow, mode, and owner — all updated in real time from OPC UA tags polled from the PLC (opc.tcp://plc:4840/arwc, namespace urn:arwc:crr:tags).

The measured actuator position (CRR.PositionPct, CRR.PositionBPct from sensors) is shown separately from the accepted controller setpoint (CRR.RequestedTargetPct, CRR.RequestedTargetBPct). Record both columns with the same UTC observation time visible in FUXA or from the historian.

Query the historian for reservoir variables at the gap end time. Build the canonical sorted JSON, derive sha256 as passphrase, and decrypt the sealed record in CairnReach/Records/ on the OT workstation to read the flag.

d2f301c4-2874-4703-88a0-5b78409f976a.name: W17.2: The mode the plant is in
d2f301c4-2874-4703-88a0-5b78409f976a.description: Use the real operator and equipment views to identify the current controller mode, command owner, field-data state, and both outlet permissives at one UTC observation time.

hints.text: The five fields come from FUXA crr-overview header and both outlet faceplates. Mode is CRR.AutoMode (false=manual), owner is CRR.Owner (0=local/HMI, 1=remote), field-data state is CRR.IoHealthy, and per-outlet permissives are CRR.PermissiveA and CRR.PermissiveB.

All five tags are in ot_history.process_samples. Query SELECT DISTINCT ON (tags->>"variable") time, tags->>"variable", fields->>"value" FROM ot_history.process_samples WHERE tags->>"variable" IN ("AutoMode","Owner","IoHealthy","PermissiveA","PermissiveB") ORDER BY tags->>"variable", time DESC.

Query the historian for mode and permissive variables at the gap end time. Build the canonical sorted JSON with integer values, derive sha256 as passphrase, and decrypt the sealed record in CairnReach/Records/ on the OT workstation.

2a93db3d-65cc-413d-8cf1-810d289b8d38.name: W17.3: The instrument in the note

hints.text: Read ~/CairnReach/Briefs/W17/engineering-reference.md (reference CRR-ENG-INST-204B-R1). It maps the outlet B flow transmitter FIT-CRR-204B to IEC variable FlowBM3s, OPC UA NodeId, historian series, and unit. The reference describes the identity but does not supply a current value or confirm quality.

Confirm in the historian catalog: SELECT variable, series, node_id, unit FROM ot_history.tag_catalog WHERE series = 'flow_b_m3s'. The result must match the reference document exactly on all five fields.
